chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Panassie's background and his plan for a jazz club
summary: Briggs says Panassie, a count who married young, wanted a club to educate the French about jazz, though he saw it as a commercial venture while Briggs and Johnson saw it as education.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All right, now, you were saying to me earlier that Panassie was kind of a wealthy kid and he had lots of money, and
Briggs 290
he could really do this -- get involved with all of this as kind of a hobby; is that correct?
I don't know about that, if that was true, 'cause Panassie, I found out that Panassie had been married really young.
He had?
Yes. And he told Freddie Johnson and I that his wife and sister were awfully mean to him, you see. They used to whip him.
His wife?
His wife and his sister, used to whip him. And then --
He was what, married when he was a kid, a little boy?
His wife -- apparently he married quite young. He must have married quite young, 'cause when I met him he was only about 21 or 22.
Briggs 291
I see.
And he said that his sister and his wife used to whip him. And he broke away from them, and met his present wife, I mean the person who became his wife, Madeline Gautier.
Right.
Madeline Gautier. And that's where we -- he asked us to come down to his apartment on the Left Bank, and we went.

And, that's where he had the recordings of Mezzrow, and an old beat-up Albert/clarinet that he tried to play to imitate Mezzrow's recordings, and he -- he expressed the idea as to how he loved jazz, and everything, he understood everything, and he loved jazz, and he would like to form a club, you know, to educate the French people, the youngsters about jazz.
Well, was he at the University, at this time?
Briggs
No, he wasn't at the University.
He wasn't?
No, no. But he was -- I will say, his name is Hugues de Panassie, that is a nobleman --
Right.
He is a count. He was a count.
Right.
And he intended to open this -- to do this Hot Club business on -- we gathered---Freddy, and I gathered -- the intent was to make a commercial business of it.
But we, we were interested in the education of the public for our profession and for those who come after us, you see.
Right.
